pr_title: [Merged by Bors] - Use prepass shaders for shadows
pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #4372.

## Solution

- Use the prepass shaders for the shadow passes.
- Move `DEPTH_CLAMP_ORTHO` from `ShadowPipelineKey` to `MeshPipelineKey` and the associated clamp operation from `depth.wgsl` to `prepass.wgsl`.
- Remove `depth.wgsl` .
- Replace `ShadowPipeline` with `ShadowSamplers`.

Instead of running the custom `ShadowPipeline` we run the `PrepassPipeline` with the `DEPTH_PREPASS` flag and additionally the `DEPTH_CLAMP_ORTHO` flag for directional lights as well as the `ALPHA_MASK` flag for materials that use `AlphaMode::Mask(_)`.
pr_comments: Thank you for catching that! Fixed it.

Until we get support for [transparent shadow maps](https://wickedengine.net/2018/01/18/easy-transparent-shadow-maps/), would it be reasonable to treat Materials with AlphaMode::Blend as if they had AlphaMode::Mask(0.5) in the context of shadow mapping? I have noticed, that many third party 3d assets generally tend to use alpha blending over alpha masking for things like foliage, even if they don't really make good use of it (maybe because alpha blending can anti-alias the edges). It's cumbersome having to modify these assets, so assuming AlphaMode::Mask(0.5) for shadows would be a decent approximation.

@pkupper Based on the observation that for `AlphaMode::Add` or `AlphaMode::Blend` and `alpha = 0.0` the blending operation will not change the currently stored color/alpha value in the fragment buffer and the fragment is therefore invisible, I decided to discard fragments with those `AlphaMode`s, if the alpha value is below `0.05`. I have chosen that value because that was the threshold below which I couldn't see the cube in the `transparency_3d` example anymore.

the code looks good. 

i wonder how a custom material would specify that it wants material bindings for the shadow fragment stage? it looks like currently it uses the mesh key alpha mode to decide; maybe that's fair but maybe we should have a custom key bit so that users can set it specifically.
Yes, I think the PR is ready to merge.

issue_context.title: Transparent base_color_texture with AlphaMode::Mask should make shadow casters transparent
issue_context.body:
In the following scene, a simple mesh is constructed from a basic plane mesh:

```rs
commands
    .spawn_bundle(PbrBundle {
        mesh: meshes.add(Mesh::from(shape::Plane { size: 1.0 })),
        material: materials.add(StandardMaterial {
            base_color_texture: Some(chara_texture.clone()),
            double_sided: false,
            alpha_mode: AlphaMode::Mask(0.5),
            ..Default::default()
        }),
        transform: Transform::from_xyz(0.0, 0.5, 0.0),
        ..Default::default()
    });
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6179181/160977835-fb9294fa-2246-45a7-970b-605c24a1272e.png)

The mesh itself is transparent ("cut out" where the alpha of the texture is more than 0.5) but the entire plane casts a shadow. This means that it casts a shadow in a different shape than the object itself.

## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?

Meshes textures with transparency using `AlphaMode::Mask` can cast shadows that match their shape in space.

## What solution would you like?

When a `StandardMaterial` has `AlphaMode::Mask`, it should automatically cast shadows using the same mask for transparency. If this is infeasible, a built-in `ShadowTextureMask{ ... }` component could be an alternative solution.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?

In some cases, the shape of the object could be constructed out of geometry instead of using textures, or a custom alternative shadow pass could be built. This would be a lot of work to match the probably "expected" behavior.

## Additional context

It's not entirely clear how shadows should behave for transparency with `AlphaMode::Blend`, so that's out-of-scope for this issue. Using a separate component (even optionally) could make this clearer, by allowing different strategies for the shadow and the mesh in the standard pipeline (e.g. blend transparency in the main pipeline, while using `AlphaMode::Mask(0.1)` for shadows).
comments: I haven’t looked into any they about how this should be done but I suspect it’s as simple as having to implement opaque and alpha mask shadow phases where the alpha mask phase has a fragment shader that discards similar to the pbr shader. I haven’t yet had to implement a fragment shader that doesn’t return anything. All this has to do is check the alpha for the fragment and discard or not. I don’t know if that is a valid fragment shader.
+1 I would love to have this
Second. Objects like foliage make heavy use of this and is a must-have.

review_comments: _Not for this PR_, but now that we read the `material` here, perhaps we could also have a per-material flag to disable casting shadows?
Oh, that's a pretty neat idea, I guess it would be less ECS friendly though, since now you'd need to query all material instead of just querying for NotShadowCaster.
